# Weighing the positions


Three positions are parties to one dispute. LST holds only what it says the
texts establish: the Spirit is related to the Son as well as to the Father. The
West, with Aquinas, Florence and Westminster, holds that he proceeds from the
Father and the Son. The East, with Photius and Ware, holds that he proceeds from
the Father alone. Who defeats whom is computed from their premises and checked
by the kernel.

## How to read the verdicts

- **Defeats.** One position contradicts another (it denies one of the other's
  premises, its conclusion, or a claim it derives on the way) and is not the
  weaker of the two. A defeat that runs both ways is a *standoff*.
- **Weakest link.** A position is only as strong as its least-supported premise
  or step. LST's weakest link is `wellSupported`. Each side rests on readings
  rated `disputed`, the lowest rating, so no rating breaks their standoff.
- **Forced.** Accepted however every standoff is resolved.
- **Can be defended.** Held by some consistent position that answers every
  attack on its members, by itself or through an ally.

## What the weighing found

One standoff, and nothing else. The West and the East defeat each other over
"and the Son", and neither attacks LST, because each grants every text LST
cites and the relation LST draws from them. So what is forced is exactly LST's
position (`the_texts_prevail`). The West can be defended, and so can the East,
and neither is forced (`western_defensible`, `western_not_forced`,
`eastern_defensible`, `eastern_not_forced`).

That is LST's grading of the question, reproduced given these ratings: the relation of the Spirit to
the Son is settled, and "the exact eternal relation of the Spirit to the Son
beyond what Scripture states is not demonstrated". It does not show that the
question is idle, or that the two sides read equally well. It shows only that
the weighing cannot choose, because every reading that divides them is rated
`disputed`. A new, cited argument that one side's reading survives what the
other side says against it could move a rating, and so the verdict. LST's own
rating plays no part: nothing attacks its position, so it would prevail at any
rating.

The standoff rests on reading "proceeds" the same way on both sides. The
Pontifical Council for Promoting Christian Unity (1995) distinguishes the
Greek ἐκπόρευσις, origin from the Father alone, from the Latin *processio*.
On that distinction "and the Son" and "not from the Son" may not contradict each
other, and the two defeats would not exist. The chapter on the procession says
what testing that would take.


## How this is checked

<details class="testimony-checked">
<summary>The positions, steps and results behind this chapter, each with the formula or the Lean that checks it</summary>

### Strength

<a id="lstCase_strength"></a>
**`lstCase_strength`**

LST's weakest link is `wellSupported`: its step from the texts to the
relation, audited for a reader who grants the texts and denies the relation,
and none found. The texts themselves are `consensus`.

```lean
theorem lstCase_strength : lstCase.strength = 2
-- axioms: propext
```

<a id="westernCase_strength"></a>
**`westernCase_strength`**

The Western position's weakest link is `disputed`: its readings of John 16:14
and of the mission, the claim that only opposed relations distinguish the
persons, and its steps from John 16:14 and from mission. Its step from
distinction is rated `wellSupported`.

```lean
theorem westernCase_strength : westernCase.strength = 0
-- axioms: propext
```

<a id="easternCase_strength"></a>
**`easternCase_strength`**

The Eastern position's weakest link is `disputed`: each of its two readings,
and each of its two steps.

```lean
theorem easternCase_strength : easternCase.strength = 0
-- axioms: propext
```

### The dispute

<a id="partyNode"></a>
**`partyNode`**

The package each party argues from.

```lean
def partyNode : Party → ArgumentPackage Claim :=
  fun x =>
    match x with
    | Party.lst => lstCase
    | Party.western => westernCase
    | Party.eastern => easternCase
```

<a id="processionDispute"></a>
**`processionDispute`**

The dispute over the procession: every party can be held without
contradiction, delivers its conclusion, and has its steps rated.

```lean
def processionDispute : Dispute Claim Party :=
  { node := partyNode, consistent := processionDispute._proof_1,
    sound := processionDispute._proof_2,
    rated := processionDispute._proof_6 }
```

<a id="lst_stands_with_the_west"></a>
**`lst_stands_with_the_west`**

**LST stands with the West**: one reading satisfies both, the Western
reading.

```lean
theorem lst_stands_with_the_west : processionDispute.StandTogether [Party.lst,
    Party.western]
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```

<a id="lst_stands_with_the_east"></a>
**`lst_stands_with_the_east`**

**LST stands with the East** too: the Eastern reading satisfies both. So
LST's position takes no side, which is what it says of itself.

```lean
theorem lst_stands_with_the_east : processionDispute.StandTogether [Party.lst,
    Party.eastern]
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```

<a id="partyDefeats"></a>
**`partyDefeats`**

The defeats of the dispute, as a table: the West and the East, each way.

```lean
def partyDefeats : Party → Party → Prop :=
  fun x x_1 =>
    match x, x_1 with
    | Party.western, Party.eastern => True
    | Party.eastern, Party.western => True
    | x, x_2 => False
```

<a id="instDecidableRelPartyPartyDefeats"></a>
**`instDecidableRelPartyPartyDefeats`**

The table is finite, so membership in it is decidable.

```lean
def instDecidableRelPartyPartyDefeats : DecidableRel partyDefeats
```

<a id="partyStrength"></a>
**`partyStrength`**

Each party's weakest link: `wellSupported` for LST, `disputed` for the two
sides.

```lean
def partyStrength : Party → ℕ :=
  fun x =>
    match x with
    | Party.lst => 2
    | x => 0
```

<a id="partyNode_strength"></a>
**`partyNode_strength`**

Each party's weakest link, as its package computes it.

```lean
theorem partyNode_strength : ∀ (i : Party), (partyNode i).strength =
    partyStrength i
-- axioms: propext
```

<a id="processionDispute_defeats"></a>
**`processionDispute_defeats`**

**Who defeats whom**, all 9 pairs: one standoff, the West and the East over
"and the Son", and nothing else. Neither attacks LST, because each holds every
premise LST holds. Every cell is checked by the kernel.

```lean
theorem processionDispute_defeats : ∀ (i j : Party), processionDispute.defeats
    i j ↔ partyDefeats i j
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```

<a id="processionFinite"></a>
**`processionFinite`**

The dispute in the form the verdict solver computes with.

```lean
def processionFinite : Solver.Finite processionDispute.defeats :=
  {
    parties :=
      [Party.lst, Party.western, Party.eastern],
    complete := processionFinite._proof_1,
    defeats := fun i j => decide (partyDefeats i j),
    spec := processionFinite._proof_2 }
```

<a id="processionDispute_supports"></a>
**`processionDispute_supports`**

**Nothing supports anything**, in all 9 pairs: no party's conclusion is a
premise another party states. LST's relation is derived inside the other two
positions, not assumed by them. Every cell is checked by the kernel.

```lean
theorem processionDispute_supports : ∀ (i j : Party),
    ¬processionDispute.supports i j
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```

<a id="partyPartOf"></a>
**`partyPartOf`**

Which party's case is part of which: LST's is part of every party's, since
each holds the texts and the step LST draws from them; otherwise each case is
part of its own only.

```lean
def partyPartOf : Party → Party → Prop :=
  fun x x_1 =>
    match x, x_1 with
    | Party.lst, x => True
    | Party.western, Party.western => True
    | Party.eastern, Party.eastern => True
    | x, x_2 => False
```

<a id="instDecidableRelPartyPartyPartOf"></a>
**`instDecidableRelPartyPartyPartOf`**

The table is finite, so membership in it is decidable.

```lean
def instDecidableRelPartyPartyPartOf : DecidableRel partyPartOf
```

<a id="processionDispute_partOf"></a>
**`processionDispute_partOf`**

**LST's case is part of both the others'.** Every cell is checked by the
kernel.

```lean
theorem processionDispute_partOf : ∀ (i j : Party), processionDispute.partOf i
    j ↔ partyPartOf i j
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```

The defeats are the cells of [`processionDispute_defeats`](#processionDispute_defeats), the supports the cells of [`processionDispute_supports`](#processionDispute_supports) and the parts the cells of [`processionDispute_partOf`](#processionDispute_partOf), each computed from the parties' premises and checked by the kernel. The attacks derived through support and through parts are reported, not counted: every verdict is computed from the defeats alone. Every derived attack is already a defeat.

### What the dispute decides

<a id="textsUnanswered"></a>
**`textsUnanswered`**

How far the dispute is settled, in one stage. Nothing defeats LST, so it
comes first, and nothing joins it: the West has the East for a defeater, the
East has the West, and LST answers neither.

**What the dispute forces is exactly *The texts: the Spirit sent by the Son and named for him*.**

- Stage 1: *The texts: the Spirit sent by the Son and named for him*.
  - *The texts: the Spirit sent by the Son and named for him* is defeated by nothing.
- Nothing else is forced:
  - *From the Father alone (Photius; Ware)* defeats *From the Father and the Son (Aquinas; Florence; Westminster)*, and nothing forced defeats *From the Father alone (Photius; Ware)*.
  - *From the Father and the Son (Aquinas; Florence; Westminster)* defeats *From the Father alone (Photius; Ware)*, and nothing forced defeats *From the Father and the Son (Aquinas; Florence; Westminster)*.

**What this rests on.** The reasons state 2 defeats and 5 absences of defeat, each a cell of the defeat table, [`processionDispute_defeats`](#processionDispute_defeats), computed from the two parties' premises and checked by the kernel. Whether an attack survives turns on the attacker's weakest link and on the rating of what it attacks, so a changed rating can change the verdict. The weakest links:

- *The texts: the Spirit sent by the Son and named for him*, weakest at *well supported*:
  - an inference step — [Kibbey 2026](../../bibliography.md#kibbey-living-systematic-theology-2026), §§3, The Triune God; [Photius 1987](../../bibliography.md#photius-mystagogy-1987); [Vischer 1981](../../bibliography.md#vischer-spirit-of-god-1981), p. 178; [Aquinas 1920](../../bibliography.md#aquinas-summa-1920), §I, q. 36, a. 2
- *From the Father and the Son (Aquinas; Florence; Westminster)*, weakest at *disputed*:
  - In John 16:14 what the Spirit takes from the Son is his being, not only his word — [Aquinas 1920](../../bibliography.md#aquinas-summa-1920), §I, q. 36, a. 2
  - The Son's sending of the Spirit rests on an eternal relation of Spirit to Son — [Aquinas 1920](../../bibliography.md#aquinas-summa-1920), §I, q. 36, a. 2; [Vischer 1981](../../bibliography.md#vischer-spirit-of-god-1981), p. 165
  - The divine persons are distinguished only by opposed relations of origin — [Aquinas 1920](../../bibliography.md#aquinas-summa-1920), §I, q. 36, a. 2
  - an inference step — [Aquinas 1920](../../bibliography.md#aquinas-summa-1920), §I, q. 36, a. 2; [Photius 1987](../../bibliography.md#photius-mystagogy-1987)
  - an inference step — [Vischer 1981](../../bibliography.md#vischer-spirit-of-god-1981), pp. 165–169; [Vischer 1981](../../bibliography.md#vischer-spirit-of-god-1981), p. 144; [Vischer 1981](../../bibliography.md#vischer-spirit-of-god-1981), pp. 183–184; [Aquinas 1920](../../bibliography.md#aquinas-summa-1920), §I, q. 43, a. 8
- *From the Father alone (Photius; Ware)*, weakest at *disputed*:
  - John 15:26 "proceeds" speaks of the Spirit's eternal origin, not only of mission — [Aquinas 1920](../../bibliography.md#aquinas-summa-1920), §I, q. 36, a. 2; [Photius 1987](../../bibliography.md#photius-mystagogy-1987)
  - In John 15:26 Jesus names the Spirit's source, the Father, and no other — [Photius 1987](../../bibliography.md#photius-mystagogy-1987); [Ware 1993](../../bibliography.md#ware-orthodox-church-1993)
  - The Father is the one cause of the Son and of the Spirit — [Photius 1987](../../bibliography.md#photius-mystagogy-1987); [Ware 1993](../../bibliography.md#ware-orthodox-church-1993)
  - an inference step — [Photius 1987](../../bibliography.md#photius-mystagogy-1987); [Aquinas 1920](../../bibliography.md#aquinas-summa-1920), §I, q. 36, a. 2
  - an inference step — [Tanner 1990](../../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Florence, Session 6 (1439), Laetentur caeli; [Pontifical Council for Promoting Christian Unity 1995](../../bibliography.md#pcpcu-greek-latin-traditions-1995); [Photius 1987](../../bibliography.md#photius-mystagogy-1987)

<a id="the_texts_prevail"></a>
**`the_texts_prevail`**

**What the texts establish prevails, and nothing more.** What the dispute
forces before any choice between rivals is exactly LST's position: the Spirit
is related to the Son as well as to the Father. Nothing defeats it, because
the West and the East both hold every premise it holds.

What this does not claim: that the Filioque is false, or that it is true. The
West and the East are in a standoff, and neither is forced.

```lean
theorem the_texts_prevail : Framework.grounded processionDispute.defeats =
    {Party.lst}
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```

***From the Father and the Son (Aquinas; Florence; Westminster)* is accepted on some resolution.**

- A position holding *The texts: the Spirit sent by the Son and named for him*, *From the Father and the Son (Aquinas; Florence; Westminster)* can be held.
- None of *The texts: the Spirit sent by the Son and named for him*, *From the Father and the Son (Aquinas; Florence; Westminster)* defeats another, and each attack on them is answered from among them:

<a id="western_not_forced"></a>
**`western_not_forced`**

**Nor is it forced.** A maximal defensible position holds LST's position and
the East's, and cannot hold the West's with them.

```lean
theorem western_not_forced : ¬Framework.SkepticallyAccepted
    processionDispute.defeats Party.western
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```

<a id="easternWithTheTexts"></a>
**`easternWithTheTexts`**

Why the East can be defended: with LST, it answers the West itself.

***From the Father alone (Photius; Ware)* is accepted on some resolution.**

- A position holding *The texts: the Spirit sent by the Son and named for him*, *From the Father alone (Photius; Ware)* can be held.
- None of *The texts: the Spirit sent by the Son and named for him*, *From the Father alone (Photius; Ware)* defeats another, and each attack on them is answered from among them:
  - *From the Father and the Son (Aquinas; Florence; Westminster)* defeats *From the Father alone (Photius; Ware)*, and *From the Father alone (Photius; Ware)* defeats *From the Father and the Son (Aquinas; Florence; Westminster)*.

**What this rests on.** The reasons state 2 defeats and 5 absences of defeat, each a cell of the defeat table, [`processionDispute_defeats`](#processionDispute_defeats), computed from the two parties' premises and checked by the kernel. Whether an attack survives turns on the attacker's weakest link and on the rating of what it attacks, so a changed rating can change the verdict. The weakest links:

- *The texts: the Spirit sent by the Son and named for him*, weakest at *well supported*:
  - an inference step — [Kibbey 2026](../../bibliography.md#kibbey-living-systematic-theology-2026), §§3, The Triune God; [Photius 1987](../../bibliography.md#photius-mystagogy-1987); [Vischer 1981](../../bibliography.md#vischer-spirit-of-god-1981), p. 178; [Aquinas 1920](../../bibliography.md#aquinas-summa-1920), §I, q. 36, a. 2
- *From the Father alone (Photius; Ware)*, weakest at *disputed*:
  - John 15:26 "proceeds" speaks of the Spirit's eternal origin, not only of mission — [Aquinas 1920](../../bibliography.md#aquinas-summa-1920), §I, q. 36, a. 2; [Photius 1987](../../bibliography.md#photius-mystagogy-1987)
  - In John 15:26 Jesus names the Spirit's source, the Father, and no other — [Photius 1987](../../bibliography.md#photius-mystagogy-1987); [Ware 1993](../../bibliography.md#ware-orthodox-church-1993)
  - The Father is the one cause of the Son and of the Spirit — [Photius 1987](../../bibliography.md#photius-mystagogy-1987); [Ware 1993](../../bibliography.md#ware-orthodox-church-1993)
  - an inference step — [Photius 1987](../../bibliography.md#photius-mystagogy-1987); [Aquinas 1920](../../bibliography.md#aquinas-summa-1920), §I, q. 36, a. 2
  - an inference step — [Tanner 1990](../../bibliography.md#tanner-decrees-1990), §Florence, Session 6 (1439), Laetentur caeli; [Pontifical Council for Promoting Christian Unity 1995](../../bibliography.md#pcpcu-greek-latin-traditions-1995); [Photius 1987](../../bibliography.md#photius-mystagogy-1987)
- *From the Father and the Son (Aquinas; Florence; Westminster)*, weakest at *disputed*:
  - In John 16:14 what the Spirit takes from the Son is his being, not only his word — [Aquinas 1920](../../bibliography.md#aquinas-summa-1920), §I, q. 36, a. 2
  - The Son's sending of the Spirit rests on an eternal relation of Spirit to Son — [Aquinas 1920](../../bibliography.md#aquinas-summa-1920), §I, q. 36, a. 2; [Vischer 1981](../../bibliography.md#vischer-spirit-of-god-1981), p. 165
  - The divine persons are distinguished only by opposed relations of origin — [Aquinas 1920](../../bibliography.md#aquinas-summa-1920), §I, q. 36, a. 2
  - an inference step — [Aquinas 1920](../../bibliography.md#aquinas-summa-1920), §I, q. 36, a. 2; [Photius 1987](../../bibliography.md#photius-mystagogy-1987)
  - an inference step — [Vischer 1981](../../bibliography.md#vischer-spirit-of-god-1981), pp. 165–169; [Vischer 1981](../../bibliography.md#vischer-spirit-of-god-1981), p. 144; [Vischer 1981](../../bibliography.md#vischer-spirit-of-god-1981), pp. 183–184; [Aquinas 1920](../../bibliography.md#aquinas-summa-1920), §I, q. 43, a. 8

<a id="eastern_defensible"></a>
**`eastern_defensible`**

**The Eastern position can be defended**, together with LST's.

<a id="easternAnsweredByTheWest"></a>
**`easternAnsweredByTheWest`**

**`eastern_not_forced`**

**Nor is it forced.** A maximal defensible position holds LST's position and
the West's, and cannot hold the East's with them.

```lean
theorem eastern_not_forced : ¬Framework.SkepticallyAccepted
    processionDispute.defeats Party.eastern
-- axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
```
